articles.description:
Description: Potential for continued admin console access past inactivity timeout
What happened?
The admin console session timeout works by recording tailnet-specific activity timestamps on login and from browser requests triggered by user activity. Previously the admin console also erroneously considered the act of switching between multiple tailnets to be a login and recorded a fresh timestamp for the user in the destination tailnet while switching.
For tailnets whose users were also members of other tailnets with less strict inactivity timeouts, these users may have been able to continue their access to the admin console for longer than expected if they switched between tailnets and did not time out of the less restrictive tailnet.
The issue was present since inactivity timeout was initially released in August 2024, and was fixed in production on March 7th, 2025. A user who switches to a tailnet in which their session has already expired will be logged out and redirected to the login page.
Who was affected?
Tailnets with admin console session timeout configurations and users who are members of other tailnets with less strict session timeout configurations.
What was the impact?
Users of tailnets with strict admin console session timeouts may have been able to continue their access to the admin console past expected timeouts by switching to and from other tailnets in the admin console whose console configurations were less strict.
What do I need to do?
No action is required.
articles.title: TS-2025-001

articles.description:
Incident began at 2025-03-25 18:00 (times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)).

Calendar users in Chile's Aysén region need to update the time zone for all events taking place after 2025-04-05 which are impacted by the new DST rules.

On 2025-03-20, Chile's Aysén region adopted a new time zone (IANA: "America/Coyhaique”). This time zone will diverge from the continental Chile time zone “Chile Time” (IANA: “America/Santiago”) after 2025-04-05, by staying at UTC-03.

Users in, or operating in, the Aysén region will be impacted: their events taking place after 2025-04-05 will be, by default, in the Chile time zone and will diverge by one hour compared to the new Aysén region local time.

Impacted users are recommended to take 2 actions as soon as possible:

  • Go to Calendar Settings > General > Time zone and set their Primary time zone to “Punta Arenas time” (IANA: "America/Punta_Arenas”).
  • Update all their events taking place after 2025-04-05 in this region to the “Punta Arenas time”.

Additionally, we are working on introducing a new time zone for the Aysén region.

We will post a communication update when it will be available in Calendar.

We will provide an update by Friday, 2025-04-04 13:00 US/Pacific with current details.

If impacted users don’t take action, after 2025-04-05 their calendar will:

  • Show the wrong time with the “Now” red line on Calendar Web;
  • Display all events shifted by one hour;
  • Create new events in the wrong time zone.

Affected products: Google Calendar

Resolved - Between March 27, 2025, 23:45 UTC and March 28, 2025, 01:40 UTC the Pull Requests service was degraded and failed to update refs for repositories with higher traffic activity. This was due to a large repository migration that resulted in a larger than usual number of enqueued jobs; while simultaneously impacting git fileservers where the problematic repository was hosted. This resulted in an increase in queue depth due to retries on failures to perform those jobs causing delays for non-migration sourced jobs.
We declared an incident once we confirmed that this issue was not isolated to the problematic migration and other repositories were also failing to process ref updates. 
We mitigated the issue by stopping the migration and short circuiting the remaining jobs. Additionally, we increased the worker pool of this job to reduce the time required to recover. 
As a result of this incident, we are revisiting our repository migration process and are working to isolate potentially problematic migration workloads from non-migration workloads.

During the incident, about 0.6% of workflow runs failed to start, 0.8% of workflow runs were delayed by an average of one hour, and 0.1% of runs ultimately ended with an infrastructure failure. However, due to an unrelated issue, there was a replication delay at the time of the incident, and failing over would have caused a greater impact on our customers. articles.description: From around 6:45 AM PST on February 26, 2025 to 8:30 AM PST on February 27, 2025, Slack users experienced issues with our Events API. Specifically, custom applications, integrations, and bots may not have worked as expected. Additionally, some users may have experienced issues with @mentioning Slack Connect channel members.This issue was a result of the mitigation measures we took while working to resolve a concurrent incident. To help us address the initial incident, we paused the Events API job queue and rate-limited a non-critical API endpoint that was generating an outsized load. While the queue was paused, incoming Events API requests were placed in a backlog. Once we stabilized the database tier and restored critical Slack functionality, we re-enabled the Events API queue at around 11:27 PM PST on February 26, 2025. From this point onwards, all new events were processed as expected. We made the decision not to replay the backlogged events to avoid confusion over significantly delayed app responses, and to avoid a surge of queued events for both our own systems and those of third-party providers. We continued working to address lingering issues with Slack Connect @mentions, fully resolving the incident for all impacted users at 8:30 AM PST on February 27, 2025.

articles.description: On March 10, 2025, from 12:47 PM PDT to 1:42 PM PDT, all users may have experienced issues with search in Slack. File, message, and channel searches did not return results, and the admin dashboard may not have loaded correctly.A misconfiguration in our search-related infrastructure caused queries to fail to resolve.To restore search behaviour, we scaled up our infrastructure and redirected incoming search requests to other servers. In parallel, we rolled back the incorrect configuration on the impacted search server. Once this was complete, we verified that the affected search server was functioning normally once again. We resumed the flow of search traffic to this server, fully resolving the issue for all users.
